name: DESI 2024 BAO cosmological constraints

summary.plain: Using the first year of DESI data, the collaboration measured the cosmic expansion history with baryon acoustic oscillations. The data fit standard flat ΛCDM on their own, but combined with CMB and supernova data they prefer dark energy that weakens with time, at 2.5σ to 3.9σ.
summary.technical: BAO from galaxy, quasar and Lyman-α forest tracers in 7 redshift bins (0.1<z<4.2, over 6 million objects) from DESI year 1 (Data Release 1). DESI BAO alone give Ωm = 0.295 ± 0.015 and w = -0.99 (+0.15, -0.13) in flat wCDM; in the w0wa model, DESI+CMB prefer w0>-1 and wa<0 at 2.6σ, rising to 2.5σ, 3.5σ or 3.9σ discrepancy with ΛCDM when Pantheon+, Union3 or DES-SN5YR supernovae are added. Neutrino mass: Σmν < 0.072 eV (95%).

title: DESI 2024 VI: Cosmological Constraints from the Measurements of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations
why_it_matters: The abstract reports that DESI BAO data alone are consistent with flat ΛCDM, while combinations with CMB and supernova data prefer a time-varying dark energy equation of state with w0 > -1 and wa < 0, discrepant with ΛCDM at the 2.5σ to 3.9σ level depending on the supernova sample.
